subtitle: How Three Traditions Wrote the Fall of Prithviraj Chauhan

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of Prithviraj III astride a horse at dusk near Tarain, two shadowy armies in the distance
panels.action: Prithviraj III sits tall on his horse on the dusty plain of Tarain, dusk light gilding his armour as distant war-banners of two hosts tremble against a darkening sky.

dialogue.text: In 1191, Prithviraj Chauhan wounded Muhammad of Ghor and held the field. In 1192, he was taken alive. How he fell became a battle of books as fierce as Tarain itself.

i18n.hi: ११९१ में पृथ्वीराज चौहान ने मोहम्मद गोरी को घायल किया और मैदान थामे रखा। ११९२ में वो ज़िंदा पकड़े गए। उनकी गिरावट खुद तराइन जितनी भयंकर किताबों की जंग बन गई।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Prithviraj’s face, contemplative, overlooking a camp near Tarain before the first battle
panels.action: Prithviraj III stands on a slight rise beside his pavilion near Tarain, brows knitted, looking out over his camp fires and lines of tents under a cold January sky.

dialogue.text: The winter of 1191 found Prithviraj, king of Ajmer and Delhi, facing a new kind of enemy from the northwest: Muhammad of Ghor, a ruler trained on the frontiers of empires.

i18n.hi: ११९१ की सर्दियों में अजमेर–दिल्ली के राजा पृथ्वीराज के सामने उत्तर–पश्चिम से नया दुश्मन था: सीमाओं पर तराशा गया शासक, मोहम्मद गोरी।

panels.shot: documentary-style map shot from above, the plains of Tarain marked between Ghazni and Ajmer
panels.action: A painterly map of northern India shows the rugged passes of the northwest, Ghazni, the plains of Tarain, and Ajmer, with stylised arrows pushing down from the mountains and up from the Rajput lands.

dialogue.text: The Ghurid sultan wanted the rich Gangetic plains. Prithviraj held the route from the passes to the heart of northern India. Tarain lay between them, a bare stage for a great test.

i18n.hi: ग़ुरी सुल्तान को गंगा के समृद्ध मैदानी इलाक़े चाहिए थे। पहाड़ियों से उत्तर भारत के दिल तक की राह पृथ्वीराज के हाथ में थी। बीच में था तराइन—नंगा मैदान, महा–परीक्षा की रंगभूमि।

panels.shot: wide battle tableau of the first Tarain clash, dust rising, a rider in foreign mail being dragged away
panels.action: On the battlefield of Tarain, armoured horsemen crash together in a storm of dust, while to one side a wounded commander in Central Asian mail is hurried away by a loyal rider shielding him.

dialogue.text: On that January day, the Rajput coalition struck hard. Delhi’s Tomara chief Govind Rai wounded Muhammad of Ghor in the arm, and a Ghurid soldier dragged his sultan out through the chaos.

i18n.hi: उस जनवरी के दिन राजपूत संगठित सेना ने जोरदार वार किया। दिल्ली के तंवर सरदार गोविंद राय ने मोहम्मद गोरी की बाँह घायल कर दी, और एक ग़ुरी सिपाही ने अफरातफरी में अपने सुल्तान को खींच कर बाहर निकाला।

panels.shot: somber medium shot of a Ghurid war council in a distant mountain city, maps and banners spread
panels.action: In a stark hall in the Afghan highlands, robed and armoured Ghurid commanders sit around carpets covered with maps, while an empty throne and a blood-stained gauntlet lie in the background.

dialogue.text: The sultan rode away wounded but alive. For over a year, say the Persian chronicles, he rebuilt his cavalry, weighed his mistakes, and planned how to trap Prithviraj the next time.

i18n.hi: सुल्तान घायल था, पर ज़िंदा निकल गया। फ़ारसी इतिहास कहते हैं, साल भर से ज़्यादा वो घुड़सवार फौज नई बना रहा था, गलतियाँ तौल रहा था, अगली बार पृथ्वीराज को फँसाने की चाल सोच रहा था।

panels.shot: quiet interior shot in Ajmer, Prithviraj listening to a court poet recite, yet distracted
panels.action: Inside a pillared hall in Ajmer, Prithviraj III sits on a low throne as a court poet declaims before him, but the king’s gaze is distant, hands tightening on the armrest.

dialogue.text: In Ajmer, a different story was being shaped. The Sanskrit court poet Jayanaka praised Prithviraj as a lion among kings, a defender of dharma. But he gives no clear account of the second Tarain.

i18n.hi: उधर अजमेर में एक अलग कहानी गढ़ी जा रही थी। संस्कृत दरबारी कवि जयनाक ने पृथ्वीराज को राजाओं में सिंह, धर्म–रक्षक बताया। लेकिन दूसरी तराइन की साफ़ तस्वीर वो भी नहीं देता।

panels.shot: night-time wide shot of the Ghurid camp near Tarain before the second battle, envoys riding out
panels.action: Under a moonlit sky near Tarain, the Ghurid camp glows with scattered fires as two mounted envoys leave the lines, heading toward the dark plain where the Chahamana tents stand unseen.

dialogue.text: Hasan Nizami, writing soon after, tells of a feigned truce before the second battle. Ghurid envoys, he claims, lulled Prithviraj’s camp while their masters prepared a dawn ring of steel.

i18n.hi: हसन नज़ामी, जो जल्द ही लिख रहा था, दूसरी जंग से पहले झूठी सुलह की कथा सुनाता है। ग़ुरी दूतों ने, वो कहता है, पृथ्वीराज का डेरा सुस्त कर दिया, जबकि उनके आका सुबह की लौहे की घेरा–बंदी रच रहे थे।

panels.shot: dawn wide shot from behind Prithviraj in his camp as distant lines of horsemen close in
panels.action: At pale dawn, Prithviraj III steps out of his pavilion, still unarmoured, as faint lines of horsemen can be seen far off in every direction, slowly tightening around the rising camp.

dialogue.text: Minhaj-i-Siraj describes the trap differently, but agrees on its effect: at Tarain in 1192, Ghurid cavalry encircled the Chahamana host. This time, the ring did not break.

i18n.hi: मिनहाज–ए–सिराज जाल को अलग तरह से बताता है, पर असर वही मानता है: ११९२ की तराइन में ग़ुरी घुड़सवारों ने चाहमान सेना को घेर लिया। इस बार घेरा टूटा नहीं।

panels.shot: chaotic mid-battle shot, Prithviraj surrounded, horse rearing, enemy riders closing
panels.action: In the thick of battle, dust veils the sky as Prithviraj’s horse rears, the king turning in all directions, ringed by advancing Ghurid riders with lances levelled, his own men scattered.

dialogue.text: Later ballads would say he died gloriously on the field. Yet both Sanskrit and Persian evidence point to something harsher: Prithviraj lost, was seized, and taken from Tarain alive.

i18n.hi: बाद की क़िस्सागोई कहती है कि वो रणभूमि में वीरगति को पहुँचे। पर संस्कृत और फ़ारसी दोनों साक्ष्य कुछ कठोर बताते हैं: पृथ्वीराज हारे, पकड़े गए और तराइन से ज़िंदा ले जाए गए।

panels.shot: somber close-up of Prithviraj bound but upright on a horse, being led away from the battlefield
panels.action: Prithviraj III sits bound but straight-backed on a led horse, his armour dusty, eyes fixed on the fading battlefield behind him as he is escorted away by silent Ghurid guards.

dialogue.text: Minhaj places his capture near the Sursuti river. The defeated king was not slain amid the noise of war, but removed in silence—his fate to be decided far from the dust of Tarain.

i18n.hi: मिनहाज उनकी गिरफ्तारी सुरसुती नदी के पास रखता है। हारा राजा युद्ध–कोलाहल में नहीं मारा गया, चुपचाप हटाया गया—उसका भाग्य तराइन की धूल से दूर तय होना था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Prithviraj entering Ajmer under watch, Ghurid banners behind him
panels.action: Under the gate of Ajmer’s fort, Prithviraj rides in with hands loosely bound, flanked by Ghurid horsemen bearing their standards, while townsfolk watch from the walls in uneasy stillness.

dialogue.text: Most accounts, even hostile ones, agree on a surprising move. Prithviraj was taken back to Ajmer and, for a brief time, reinstated as a subordinate ruler under the Ghurid sultan.

i18n.hi: ज़्यादातर वर्णन, दुश्मन वाले भी, एक चौंकाने वाली चाल पर सहमत हैं। पृथ्वीराज को फिर अजमेर लाया गया और थोड़े समय के लिए ग़ुरी सुल्तान के अधीन अधीनस्थ राजा बना कर बैठाया गया।

panels.shot: interior throne room shot in Ajmer, Prithviraj on a reduced seat, a Ghurid official standing over him
panels.action: In the hall at Ajmer, Prithviraj sits on a smaller, plainer throne than before, with a stern Ghurid governor standing nearby and scribes recording, while Rajput nobles watch in tight-lipped resentment.

dialogue.text: Here, power was a bargain, not a romance. A defeated king could still rule his city—so long as he accepted tribute and Ghurid oversight. Ajmer’s throne was now a test of obedience.

i18n.hi: यहाँ शक्ति सौदा थी, प्रेम–कथा नहीं। हारा हुआ राजा भी अपना शहर चला सकता था—बस ख़िराज दे और ग़ुरी निगरानी माने। अब अजमेर की गद्दी आज्ञाकारिता की परीक्षा थी।

panels.shot: tense medium shot of Prithviraj in counsel with his chiefs at night, maps and weapons set aside
panels.action: Late at night in Ajmer, Prithviraj sits with his leading chiefs around a low table, their faces lit by lamplight, maps rolled aside, hands resting uneasily on sheathed swords.

dialogue.speaker: prithviraj_iii
dialogue.text: A crown under another’s shadow—what is that to a Chahamana?

i18n.hi: किसी और की छाया में ताज—चाहमान के लिए इसकी क्या कीमत?

panels.shot: documentary montage shot: one frame of a Persian scribe, another of a Sanskrit poet, back-to-back
panels.action: Split across the panel, a Persian court scribe sits cross-legged, ink and paper before him, while opposite a Sanskrit poet in Ajmer writes on palm-leaf, their backs turned to each other.

dialogue.text: Persian chronicles say Prithviraj rebelled and was executed. Sanskrit verses hint at resistance but go quiet on his end. Each side described disloyalty and punishment in words that served its court.

i18n.hi: फ़ारसी तवारिख कहते हैं पृथ्वीराज ने बगावत की और मारे गए। संस्कृत श्लोक विरोध की झलक तो देते हैं पर उनके अंत पर मौन हो जाते हैं। हर पक्ष ने बेवफ़ाई और सज़ा को अपने दरबार की ज़ुबान दी।

panels.shot: somber shot in Ajmer’s fort courtyard, Prithviraj being led away under guard, faces watching from above
panels.action: In the stone courtyard of Ajmer’s fort, Prithviraj III walks between armed guards toward an inner passage, head high, as his nobles watch from the battlements, their expressions a mix of anger and helplessness.

dialogue.text: No eyewitness account survives of his last moments. Later Muslim writers record a formal execution. Sanskrit tradition lets him fade mid-resistance. The man disappears behind the needs of narrative.

i18n.hi: उनके आख़िरी पलों का कोई आँखों–देखा बयान नहीं बचा। बाद के मुस्लिम लेखक औपचारिक फाँसी लिखते हैं। संस्कृत परंपरा उन्हें संघर्ष के बीच धुंधला कर देती है। आदमी कथानक की ज़रूरतों के पीछे ओझल हो जाता है।

panels.shot: dramatic storytelling shot: an old bard by fire at night, audience listening rapt as he gestures an arrow’s flight
panels.action: By a village fire centuries later, an old bard stands with bow in hand, miming the release of an invisible arrow toward a distant listener, while villagers and warriors sit rapt around him.

dialogue.text: Much later, the Prithviraj Raso turned defeat into legend: a blinded king in Ghazni, a sound-guided arrow, the sultan slain. But Muhammad of Ghor died years later, elsewhere. The dates do not fit the song.

i18n.hi: बहुत बाद में, पृथ्वीराज रासो ने हार को दंतकथा बना दिया: ग़ज़नी में आँखे फूटा राजा, आवाज़ से निशाना साधा तीर, सुल्तान ढेर। पर मोहम्मद गोरी सालों बाद, कहीं और मरा—तारीख़ें गीत से मेल नहीं खातीं।

panels.shot: balanced shot of three books laid out: palm-leaf manuscript, Persian codex, printed modern history
panels.action: On a plain wooden table lie a palm-leaf manuscript with Sanskrit script, an ornate Persian codex, and a modern printed history book, their pages half-open, edges touching.

dialogue.text: Cynthia Talbot and other historians sift these clashing voices. They find agreement on place, dates, and capture—but not on motive or manner of death. Between pride and piety, the man himself is hard to see.

i18n.hi: सिंथिया टैल्बॉट और दूसरे इतिहासकार इन टकराती आवाज़ों को छानते हैं। जगह, तारीख और गिरफ्तारी पर तो मेल मिलता है—इरादे और मौत के तरीक़े पर नहीं। अहंकार और आस्था के बीच असली आदमी धुंधला पड़ जाता है।

panels.shot: wide contemporary shot of Tarain’s plain at sunset, empty fields and a distant highway
panels.action: At sunset on the flat fields around modern Taraori, green crops sway under a fading sky, with a distant road carrying trucks and buses where war-horses once charged.

dialogue.text: Today, Tarain is crossed by highways, not armies. Yet the questions born here—how we remember a fallen ruler, whose version we trust—still travel with us in every story of power and loss.

i18n.hi: आज तराइन से सेनाएँ नहीं, हाइवे गुज़रते हैं। लेकिन यहाँ उठे सवाल—गिरे हुए शासक को कैसे याद करें, किसका बयान माने—हर सत्ता और हार की कहानी के साथ हमारे साथ चलते हैं।

panels.shot: final reflective close-up of a sculpted or painted image of Prithviraj, half in light, half in shadow
panels.action: A later-era painting of Prithviraj III hangs on a rough wall, his face half lit and half in shadow, as unseen light flickers across the surface like a wavering memory.

dialogue.text: Prithviraj’s true last hour is lost, but the struggle over it endures. His fate shows how, when a king falls, chroniclers, poets, and modern scholars all rush in—each unveiling and veiling him at once.

i18n.hi: पृथ्वीराज का असली आख़िरी घंटा खो गया, पर उसकी छीना–झपटी आज भी जारी है। उनकी किस्मत दिखाती है कि जब कोई राजा गिरता है, तो इतिहासकार, कवि और आधुनिक विद्वान सब दौड़ पड़ते हैं—एक साथ उसे उजागर भी करते हैं और ओझल भी।

title_i18n.en: Tarain and the Fate of the Last Chahamana
title_i18n.hi: तराइन और आख़िरी चाहमान का मुक़द्दर

subtitle_i18n.hi: तीन परंपराओं ने कैसे लिखी पृथ्वीराज चौहान की हार
